<!-- pr-reviewer: 7755370b28d0e47b82fef230c7a37ae2a7d31788 -->
**Verdict: Ready for the maintainer to merge once `main` is merged in again (no code findings). The PR now conflicts with `main`.**

Built and tested locally at head `7755370b2` (the earlier review of this head was "read, not built"; this one builds it).

What looks good
- Clean-room: header and `docs/decisions/2482-mach3-post.md` name public sources only (Mach3Mill manual word list, RS-274); derived from our own `grblhal.cps`.
- Refusal law kept: no-feed cycle, G83 with dwell, tapping, G41/G42 and probing are refused by name; spindle-stopped check precedes each cycle; #2360 sticky-P and #1682 first-move rules carried (`mach3.cps:681-737`).
- `dwellInMilliseconds` converts P in one function (`secs`, `mach3.cps:674`).
- Body, `Changelog:`, decision file, `Fixes #2482` present; no `CHANGELOG.md`, snapshot PNG or process-file edits; no new dependency.

Results (locally, PR head as pushed - see conflicts below)
- `camcraft-post` tests: script_mach3 11, bore_cycle 9, dwell_cycles_modal_p 5, comp 9, comment_escape 3, declared_options 3, end_units 3, fanuc_post 12 - all pass.
- `camcraft-app` tests: conformance 7, after_op 10, control_comp 5, wear_comp 5, post_spindle_rule_all 5 - all pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Hand-resolved hunks checked: `bore_cycle.rs:35` `SECONDS` = tormach, grblhal, linuxcnc, mach3, and `ZERO_DWELL_P0` (line 37) unchanged, so mach3 is asserted to write no P on a zero-dwell G86 (lines 178-188); `dwell_cycles_modal_p.rs:21-29` `POSTS` length 7 with `("mach3","P0.5","P0.75")`, and `&POSTS[3..]` still covers the LinuxCNC family plus mach3. Both are correct.

Conflicts
- A trial merge with current `upstream/main` (ed581389c) conflicts in test list lines only: `after_op.rs`, `conformance.rs`, `control_comp.rs`, `wear_comp.rs`, `comment_escape.rs`, `comp.rs`, `fanuc_post.rs` (shared list lines, e.g. with #2506). Not merged locally; the merged tree was not built. The refresh is done at merge time (`/resolve-conflicts`, keep both sides) and the targeted gate is owed on the merged tree because the diff posts new G-code.

Zero-dwell G86: P0 or no P?
- Decision: omitting P is correct for Mach3; no change requested. #2362's rule is the LinuxCNC/RS274NGC one (a G86 block with no P is a control error there), which is why only tormach, grblhal and linuxcnc are in `ZERO_DWELL_P0`. The decision file and the Mach3 cycle word list name no such requirement, and the post matches Haas/Fanuc-style behaviour (`NO_DWELL`) for the no-dwell case. The sticky-P hazard is covered separately: a changed dwell reopens the cycle (`sig` includes `secs(dwell)`, `mach3.cps:723`).

Questions / notes (not blocking)
- Not run on a Mach3 control: whether Mach3 keeps an earlier P across `G80` and then a bare G86 (0.5 s hole followed by a 0 s hole) is unconfirmed. If a Mach3 user can check it, writing `P0` would be the safe change for that sequence; say so on the PR.
- Windows-only readings: none touched.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
